newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal share boom must be nearing end.
newsitem.headline: Portugal share boom must be nearing end.

text.p: A dramatic surge in Portuguese stocks, triggered by the upgrading of the bourse by the international investors' Bible, the Morgan Stanley index, must be nearing its end, analysts said on Monday.

Some stocks have soared as much as 15 percent in the two sessions since Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI), whose ratings are widely followed by big international funds, announced that Portugal had finally made the jump from emerging to developed market.

The sharp gains have taken the overall rise in the PSI20 index of leading blue chips to some 32 percent so far this year, bringing it within striking distance of the 40 percent gain which many analysts had been predicting for the whole of 1997.
The PSI20 was gaining 1.8 percent on Monday having risen 4.4 percent on Friday.

With the whole year forecasts having already taken account of a Morgan Stanley upgrade at some stage in the year, analysts said the market's ceiling must be approaching and that further progress on prices would be only gradual.
"I have not changed my forecast for a rise of between 35 and 40 percent for 1997 with the announcement (of the MSCI change)," said Jose Freire of Espirito Santo Research (ESR).

James Harrison of Lisbon brokers Midas Corretora said he was also sticking to the view, held since the beginning of the year, that the Lisbon bourse general index (BVL) could rise over 40 percent. The BVL has lagged the PSI and is showing a gain of some 28 percent so far in 1997.
"The confirmation of the (MSCI) news speeded the entry of the bigger investors which had in any case been foreseen for this year," he said.
The upgrade from emerging to developed in the MSCI indices will almost automatically draw funds to Portugal which previously ignored the country, analysts said.

The enthusiasm has focused on leading blue chips such as retailer and property group Sonae Investimentos, Portugal Telecom (PT), cement maker Cimpor, retailer Jeronimo Martins and various banks, most notably Banco Comercial Portugues.
But some analysts felt that the market's response to the MSCI decision, announced on Wednesday night, had been excessive.
Joao Vermelho of Central de Investimentos said he was sticking to a forecast for overall growth in the stock market index of 15 to 20 percent in 1997.
"There is a great deal of euphoria at the moment...the reaction has been very violent," he said. The analyst said that he now expected to see a correction after the big advance.
